messages:
anna: Heads-up — thinking about adding a "signal priority" layer to how console SLO alerts are routed. Not just tenant -> team, but classifying by signal (latency/error/throughput) and routing to different escalation tiers.
raj: Interesting. Is that mainly to reduce noise or to get the right inbox faster?
anna: Both. For example: a high-rate 429 storm should go to infra oncall first (auto-silence to product), whereas an intermittent p95 latency spike should open an ops+product dialog.
kim: How would we encode that in the API? Per-route metadata or an additional routingPolicy resource?
raj: I was picturing a routingPolicy object attached to SLOs. e.g.
```
routingPolicy:
  priority: high
  signalType: rate_limit
  primary: infra-oncall
  fallback: infra-async
  quiet_window: 10m
  sample_telemetry: low
```
mike: We need to be careful with quiet_window. If we set it globally for rate signals we might miss real regressions. Maybe allow a graceFactor that decays based on historical baselines.
sylvia: Also need to consider per-tenant quotas. High-volume tenants should get rate-aggregated alerts (grouped) rather than per-route. Otherwise product teams drown.
anna: Agreed. Proposal: routing policy supports tenant_mode: [aggregate, per-tenant] and a quota_weight that influences fanout rate.
kim: Telemetry sampling is key — we don't want full traces on every routed alert. Could be sample rules like: rate signals -> 1% traces, latency p95 -> 10%.
raj: Can we wire that into the console UI as a compact toggle? UX ask from CS last week. They want a per-alert preview showing estimated alert volume and telemetry cost.
mike: That's doable if we compute expected volume from recent windows. We'll need a small estimator service (or reuse the sampling sim) and a cost column.
sylvia: Any thoughts on rollout behavior? If we change routing policy for a model SLO, we should canary it to a subset of tenants. Otherwise we risk blinding an entire product.
anna: Yes — add rollout: {percent: 10, duration: 1h, monitor: error_budget_delta}. If the delta is negative revert.
raj: One internal API question — do we version routingPolicy or make it immutable and create new revisions? For audit & rollback I prefer immutable resources + references on SLO.
kim: Immutable sounds safer. Console can show history diff.
deply-bot: deploy queued: routing-policy-service v2 -> staging (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:
mike: Let's also add a console preview that shows simulated alerts given current traffic. Quick POC: run a 24h replay and surface expected fanout numbers.
sylvia: If we're simulating, we should surface false-positive rate estimate (based on eval prompt sets for modelled signals). Helps teams tune thresholds.
anna: OK next steps: raj + kim draft routingPolicy schema; mike + sylvia prototype simulator & estimator; I'll mock a compact console preview (no modal, inline expander). Ping me in #devex when drafts ready. :thumbsup:
kim: Will do. I'll start a small RFC PR and link demo data.
raj: I'll sketch the API shape and versioning plan.
mike: I'll wire up sampling knobs to the estimator.
sylvia: I'll coordinate with CS on the UX preview wording and expected metrics.
anna: Thanks — aim to sync Tues standup, otherwise async updates here.
